item.title: Police Seek Public’s Help Identifying Man in Waikoloa Assault Investigation
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: Hawai‘i Island police are requesting the public’s assistance in identifying a male suspect who is wanted for questioning in connection with an alleged assault that occurred on April 10, 2026, at a resort condominium in the 69-200 block of Waikoloa Beach Drive.
item.content:encoded:
Hawai‘i Island police are requesting the public’s assistance in identifying a male suspect who is wanted for questioning in connection with an alleged assault that occurred on April 10, 2026, at a resort condominium in the 69-200 block of Waikoloa Beach Drive.

The suspect, pictured in the accompanying photographs, is described as a six-foot tall Caucasian male in his mid-20s.

Police ask anyone who witnessed the incident or has information that may assist with the investigation, to please contact Detective Aaron Yamanaka of the Area II Juvenile Aid Section at (808) 326-4646, ext. 3304, or via email at Aaron.Yamanaka@hawaiipolice.gov.

Tipsters who prefer to remain anonymous may call Crime Stoppers at (808) 961-8300. Crime Stoppers information is kept confidential, and tipsters may be eligible for a reward of up to $1,000.

item.title: Police Investigating Body Found in Nāʻālehu
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: The Hawai‘i Police Department is investigating the death of an unidentified man in his 60s whose remains were located in a pasture off Highway 11 near the 63-mile marker in the Ka‘ū district.
item.content:encoded:
The Hawai‘i Police Department is investigating the death of an unidentified man in his 60s whose remains were located in a pasture off Highway 11 near the 63-mile marker in the Ka‘ū district.

Police were asked to conduct a welfare check for an individual on Monday, August 17, 2026, at 3:40 p.m. Police immediately initiated search efforts, however were unable to locate him. His remains were discovered in a pasture by area residents on Tuesday, August 18, at 2:50 p.m. and reported to police.

Based on the preliminary investigation, police believe the death appears to be related to the effects of Hurricane Lala and the extreme weather conditions associated with the storm. Foul play is not suspected at this time.

Positive identification of the deceased is pending. An autopsy will be scheduled to determine the exact cause of death. Anyone with information that may assist with the investigation is asked to contact Detective Donovan Kohara of the Area II Criminal Investigation Section at (808) 326-4646, ext. 3238, or by email at donovan.kohara@hawaiipolice.gov.

item.title: Two Coffee With a Cop Events in Kona Postponed
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: The Hawai‘i Police Department’s Kona Community Policing Section has postponed two Coffee With a Cop events scheduled for this week in West Hawai‘i as officers focus their efforts on Hurricane Lala recovery operations and the department’s “Fill a Cruiser” Kōkua events.
item.content:encoded:
The Hawai‘i Police Department’s Kona Community Policing Section has postponed two Coffee With a Cop events scheduled for this week in West Hawai‘i as officers focus their efforts on Hurricane Lala recovery operations and the department’s “Fill a Cruiser” Kōkua events.

The events, originally scheduled for Wednesday, August 19, at Caffé Florian, 81-6637 Hawaii Belt Road in Kealakekua, and Thursday, August 20, at Kona Coffee & Tea in the Kona Coast Shopping Center, 74-5588 Palani Road, in Kailua-Kona, will be rescheduled at a later date.

Additional information, including the new dates and times, will be announced once they are confirmed.

The Hawai‘i Police Department appreciates the community’s understanding and continued support as officers and community partners work to assist individuals and families affected by Hurricane Lala.

item.title: Hawai‘i Police Department Holding “Fill a Police Cruiser” Kokua Events in Kona and Hilo August 20 to Support Hurricane Lala Recovery Efforts
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: In response to the extraordinary challenges facing the community following the devastating impacts of Hurricane Lala, the Hawai‘i Police Department will hold three “Fill a Cruiser” Kokua events in Kona and Hilo on Thursday, August 20, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
In response to the extraordinary challenges facing the community following the devastating impacts of Hurricane Lala, the Hawai‘i Police Department will hold three “Fill a Cruiser” Kokua events in Kona and Hilo on Thursday, August 20, 2026. The department’s Kona and Hilo community policing sections are partnering with local businesses and community organizations to collect essential supplies for individuals and families affected by the hurricane.

In Kailua-Kona, the Kona Community Policing Section is partnering with Kona Costco, Kona Walmart, The Food Basket (Hawai‘i Island’s Food Bank), Friends of First Responders, and KAPA Radio personality Tommy Ching to host two “Fill a Cruiser” events simultaneously from 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the entrances of the following stores:

  • Kona Costco, 73-5600 Maiau Street
  • Kona Walmart,  75-1015 Henry Street

In Hilo, the Hilo Community Policing Section is partnering with Safeway Hilo, the Food Basket, and Vibrant Hawaii. The “Fill a Cruiser” event will be held from 12 p.m. to 6 p.m. at:

  • Hilo Safeway, 381 E. Maka‘ala Street

A blue-and-white marked police cruiser will be stationed at each location. Community members are encouraged to donate food, water, and basic living necessities, including diapers, infant formula, and personal hygiene products with the goal of filling the police cruisers to capacity with much-needed supplies.

All donated items and monetary contributions will be distributed by the Food Basket to individuals and families in need throughout Hawai‘i Island.

The Hawai‘i Police Department and its community partners encourage everyone to participate in this meaningful event. Your kōkua and generosity will make a significant difference in the lives of many individuals and families across our island.

For more information on the Kona events, please contact Officer Dwayne Sluss of the Kona Community Policing Section at 808-326-4646 ext. 3259 or via email at dwayne.sluss@hawaiipolice.gov.

For information about the Hilo event, please contact Hilo Community Policing Officer Christopher Barto, at (808) 961-8849 or by email at Christopher.barto@hawaiipolice.gov.

item.title: Police Identify Woman Found Deceased in Ka‘ū
item.dc:creator: Kaipo Aurello
item.description: The Hawai‘i Police Department is reporting the death of 93-year-old May Doi, who was located deceased in the Ka‘ū District.
item.content:encoded:
The Hawai‘i Police Department is reporting the death of 93-year-old May Doi, who was found deceased in the Ka‘ū District.

Doi was last seen on Friday, August 14, 2026, at a residence in the 95-1100 block of Maia Street in the Nāʻālehu town subdivision. Due to the extreme weather conditions associated with Hurricane Lala, Doi was reported missing to police on Sunday, August 16, 2026, at 11 a.m.

Officers and emergency personnel immediately initiated a search for Doi. She was located deceased on Monday, August 17, at 12:30 p.m.

The circumstances surrounding Doi’s death remain under investigation. Based on the preliminary investigation, police believe her death may be related to the effects of Hurricane Lala and the extreme weather conditions associated with the storm. Foul play is not suspected.

An autopsy is scheduled for later this week to determine the exact cause of death.

Anyone with information regarding this incident is asked to please contact Detective Donovan Kohara of the Area II Criminal Investigation Section at (808) 326-4646, ext. 3238, or by email at donovan.kohara@hawaiipolice.gov.

item.title: Police Report 911 Service Number is Non Operational
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: The Hawai‘i Police Department reports that the 911 Emergency Service Number is not working. If you need police, fire, or ambulance service, and have a call phone please call (808) 961-8336. If you have a landline, please call (808) 935-3311.
item.content:encoded:
(Update as of 8.17.26 at 10:15 a.m.)

The Hawai‘i Police Department reports that the 911 Emergency Service Number is still not operational. However, text to 911 is operational. If using a cell Phone and the text to 911 does not work or if you are using a landline, Please call the non-emergency line at (808) 935-3311. There is no estimated time for restoration of 911 at this time. We will keep you updated once 911 is operational.

Original release:

The Hawai‘i Police Department reports that the 911 Emergency Service Number is not working. If you need police, fire, or ambulance service, and have a call phone please call (808) 961-8336. If you have a landline, please call (808) 935-3311.

Your safety is our top priority. Thank you for your understanding and cooperation.

item.title: Ocean View Man Killed in Two Car Crash
item.dc:creator: dlaitinen
item.description: The Hawaiʻi Police Department is investigating a two-vehicle traffic collision that claimed the life of a 45-year-old Ocean View man early Saturday afternoon, August 15, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
The Hawaiʻi Police Department is investigating a two-vehicle traffic collision that claimed the life of a 45-year-old Ocean View man early Saturday afternoon, August 15, 2026.

At 1:17 p.m., Hawaiʻi Police Department officers responded to a motor vehicle collision near the intersection of Aloha Boulevard and Lehua Lane in the Hawaiian Ocean View Estates subdivision.

Preliminary investigation indicates that a gold 2021 Kia Seltos, operated by a 45-year-old man from Hawaiian Ocean View Estates, was traveling westbound (makai) on Aloha Boulevard when it crossed over the centerline and collided head-on with a silver 2000 Nissan Altima. The Nissan was operated by a 21-year-old woman, also from Hawaiian Ocean View Estates.

The 45-year-old man was not wearing a seat belt at the time of the collision. He was pronounced dead at the scene at 1:35 p.m.

The 21-year-old woman was transported to the Kona Community Hospital, where she remains in critical condition.

The Area II Traffic Enforcement Unit has initiated a coroner’s inquest investigation. The identity of the deceased is being withheld pending notification of next of kin. The investigation into this crash remains ongoing at this time. It is unknown if the storm played a role in this crash.

Anyone who witnessed the collision or who has information regarding this incident is asked to please contact Officer Adam Roberg at (808) 326-4646, extension 3229, or email at adam.roberg@hawaiipolice.gov.

This is the 22nd traffic fatality on Hawaiʻi Island in 2026, compared to 14during the same period last year.
